basis: Carcinoma arising in the pharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Defining skeletal dysplasia and retinal degeneration; intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 30-79%.
Isolated developmental abnormality of the eye.
Infertility from abnormal sperm morphology is confined to the reproductive system.
Malignant epithelial tumour originating in the colon or rectum.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder with defining lactic acidosis; variable neurologic and respiratory manifestations lack evidence of common direct organ damage.
Inherited phagocyte oxidative-burst dysfunction; recurrent organ infections are separately diagnosed, and isolated case frequencies do not establish common intrinsic damage.
Mitochondrial myopathy and cerebellar disease; pigmentary retinopathy defines the syndrome. Hearing impairment in 30-79% omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Hereditary motor neuron disease; left ventricular hypertrophy reported in 2/6 (~33%), with limited precision. Muscle wasting reflects denervation.
Premature fusion of one lambdoid skull suture; isolated skeletal disorder.
Glial tumour arising in the brainstem.
Proteasome-related autoinflammation with neutrophilic skin infiltration; thrombocytopenia in 2/2. Seizure in 1/2 does not establish persistent neurologic damage.
Proline metabolism defect; annotated ID 20/20, seizures 13/19 and nephropathy 30-79% support involvement, although the definition notes often benign disease.
Defined by paraneoplastic involvement of joints, bones, muscles or connective tissue; an immune mechanism is not universal across this umbrella.
Inherited glycan-processing defects; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in most forms (>30%). Other organ damage varies substantially across subtypes.
Viral infection directly causing encephalitis and spinal motor-neuron injury; denervation-related muscle wasting is secondary to neurologic damage.
Cardiac, ectodermal and neurodevelopmental disease define CFC; ptosis occurs in 13/20 (65%). Frequent skeletal abnormalities omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Skeletal dysplasia with limb shortening, abnormal long bones and elbow dislocation; intellectual disability and cardiovascular malformations are occasional (<30%).
Inflammation of a single peripheral nerve; the concept does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Obstetric ectopic implantation; the umbrella does not specify direct involvement of any particular organ within the axes.
Defining neurodevelopmental and movement disorder; esotropia affects 3/7 (~43%), impairing ocular alignment. Reflux is a separately diagnosed condition.
Growth hormone-unresponsive growth disorder with hypoglycemia; hearing impairment and intellectual disability lack frequencies or established major-criterion status.
Defined by skin, hair and nail dysplasia plus missing and malformed teeth; photophobia alone does not establish ocular damage.
Viral infection located in the upper or lower respiratory tract.
Localized atrophic, hyperpigmented skin lesions without established systemic involvement.
